## STRATEGIES & INSIGHTS

[sai-00001] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: For every asset, build an exhaustive eligibility matrix covering each available category-specific exemption and each broad wildcard or general-property exemption. A specific match does not displace an independently applicable general provision.
## FORMULAS & CALCULATIONS

[calc-00002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For an independently evaluated asset-exemption pair with asset value V and statutory cap C, report claim_value = min(V, C). If the provision states no monetary cap, report V. Do not reject an otherwise eligible asset merely because V exceeds C.
[calc-00010] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For a jointly owned asset of value V held equally by n debtors, when the governing statute expressly applies separately or permits combination, calculate combined protection as min(V, Σ min(V/n, C_i)), where C_i is each debtor’s available cap. Do not automatically multiply a cap when the statute supplies one shared household or marital limit.

[err-00005] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Do not confuse aggregate ceilings with per-item ceilings, and do not import a cap from a neighboring subsection. Read the scope and limit from the exact cited provision.

Opt-out/election rules, separate-debtor rules, and a homestead provision whose unused amount enlarges a wildcard may guide the analysis without themselves covering the asset; output only provisions whose property scope directly includes it.

[ph-00003] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Apply a fixed sequence: honor the solved jurisdiction and any opt-out rule; classify the asset from explicit use facts; test all specific provisions; test all 'any property' provisions; calculate each claim independently; then deduplicate and validate the output.
